2  JUDGMENT 1.
The claimants are in appeal challenging not only the exoneration of liability on the insurer , but are also seeking for enhancement of compensation for the death of Manikanta, 19 years old.

2. The father and sister of Manikanta filed a claim petition contending that when Manikanta was riding pillion in a motor cycle there was a collision with another motor cycle, as a result of which, he sustained grievous injuries and ultimate succumbed to the same.
Initially it was stated that claim petition was filed only against the rider of the offending vehicle bearing KA-50/E-0681.

It is stated that offending vehicle did not have insurance and thereafter applications were made to implead the insurer of the motor cycle bearing No.KA-05/HA-174 on which Manikanta was riding pillion.
3.
The learned counsel for the insurer contends that when the charge sheet was laid against the rider of the motor cycle which did not have insurance, the insurer would not be liable at all.

4. On the other hand, the claimants contend that it was open for the claimants to array the tortfeasor as per their choice in the light of the Three Judge Full Bench judgment in the case of Khenyei vs.
New India Assurance Company Limited and Others - (2015)9 SCC 273 .

entities.text:
Khenyei vs.
New India Assurance Company Limited and Others - (2015)9 SCC 273
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 5. The Tribunal, in this case, on analysis of the evidence has recorded a finding that the involvement of the motor cycle bearing Reg. No.KA-05/HA-174 had not been established.
It is also stated that the claimants had failed to prove that there was head on collision between two motor cycles.

If this finding is correct, then the insurer would be liable to pay the compensation in respect of the pillion rider as it would not make any difference as to whether the other vehicle was insured or not since the Hon'ble Supreme Court had held that it was open for the claimants to choose to proceed against a tortfeasor of their choice.

Since the Tribunal has recorded a clear finding that collision between the motor cycle in which the deceased was riding and the other motor cycle which do not have insurance had not been established, it will have to be held that the insurer of the motor cycle on which the deceased was riding would be liable for compensation.
Consequently, the finding of the Tribunal that the insurer is not liable to pay the compensation is set aside and it is held that respondent No.3 insurer will be liable for the compensation.
6. The Tribunal in para 33 of this judgment has, however, stated that the accident had occurred due to wrongful act on the part of the rider of the motor cycle which do not have any licence.

The Tribunal, in one breath has stated that the motor cycle without the insurance was not involved in the accident and in another breath it has stated that it was the rider of this motor cycle which was responsible for the accident.

This clear contradiction in the award of the Tribunal would lead to the inference that the motor cycle on which the deceased was riding would have to bear the responsibility of the liability, since the vehicle was insured with a comprehensive policy.
7. As far as compensation is concerned, the Tribunal has assessed the notional income at Rs.7,000/-.

Since there was no credible documentary evidence to ascertain the actual monthly income, it would be appropriate and prudent to adopt the monthly income determined by Karnataka State Legal Services Authority, which, for the accident of the year 2015, would be Rs.9,000/-.

3
8. Since the deceased was aged 19 years, 40% is required to be added to the monthly income towards future prospects, which would result in the income to be Rs.12,600/-.
As the claimant is bachelor, if 50% is deducted towards personal expenses, his monthly income would be Rs.6,300/-.
9. The income of the deceased for the purposes of determining the loss of dependency would thus be Rs.6,300/-.
10. As the deceased was aged 19 years, a multiplier of '18' would have to be applied.

Consequently,
the claimants would be entitled to a sum of Rs.13,60,800/- (Rs.6,300/- x 12 x 18) towards 'loss of dependency'.
11.

The claimants being the father and sister of the deceased, they would each be entitled to a sum of Rs.44,000/- towards 'loss of consortium' i.e., in all Rs.88,000/- and they would also be entitled to a sum of Rs.33,000/- under the 'conventional heads'.

12. Thus, the claimants, in modification of the impugned award, would be entitled to the following sums :
 Sl. Amount  No. Particulars (in Rs.)
 1. Loss of dependency 13,60,800/-
 Loss of consortium 88,000/-
 2.
 (Rs.44,000/- x 2)
 3.
Conventional heads 33,000/-

Thus, the claimants would be entitled for compensation of Rs.14,81,800/- as against Rs.10,88,400/- awarded by the Tribunal, along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization.
14. The Insurance Company is directed to deposit the amount of compensation awarded within a period of two months from the date of receipt of a certified copy of this judgment.
15. On deposit of the compensation amount together with interest, the amount is apportioned to the father and sister of deceased in the ratio of 70:30.

4

16. Out of the share amount of compensation of the father of deceased, 70% of the compensation amount shall be deposited in the name of father of deceased in any Nationalised Bank of his choice for a period of five years and remaining 30% of the amount shall be released to him on proper identification without any further proceedings.
He is at liberty to withdraw the periodical interest accrued on his deposit from time to time.
17. The share amount of compensation of sister of the deceased shall be deposited in her name in any Nationalised or Schedule Bank of the choice of her father for a period of five years.
She is entitled to withdraw the amount of compensation within a period of five years only for the purpose of her marriage or for her further studies.
Claimant - father is entitled to withdraw the periodical interest accrued thereon from time to time.
The appeal is accordingly allowed in part.
